# Suzhou Housing Flood C-end
A uni-app H5 frontend for Suzhou housing flood-prevention services, switched from demo to real-backend remote mode with passing E2E on 2026-11-03.

## Architecture and backend
- Remote mode connects to service-expand 9610 at `/v2.0/safety/flood/*` and auth service 9211
- Deployed via nginx reverse proxy at http://127.0.0.1:8095 with /api-flood to 9610 and /api-auth to 9211 to avoid browser CORS
- Login credentials user `zsbase` / password `Zs@2026Aa!` (also the AES vector); `.env` added to .gitignore to avoid committing the password

## Auth and encryption
- Login uses pure-JS AES-256-CBC; vector `Zs@2026Aa!` yields ciphertext `H03W0LoMA6EFQZIW46BnNA==`, aligned with backend AESUtil
- request.ts injects `zhi-project-id: suzhufang` and Bearer token, unwraps `{code,msg,data}` envelope

## Key implementation
- src/stores/flood.ts implements remote mode: login / fetchTemplate / searchComplex / submitInspection / submitRescue / fetchHistoryPage / countHistory / getRecordAsync; drafts stay local, demo behavior preserved
- Four pages (inspection / detail / history / rescue) rebuilt by teammate fe-pages; E2E spec by teammate e2e-dev
- 19-digit snowflake IDs must be sent as String (see snowflake_id_precision_loss)
- Fixed history to detail navigation bug where `kind` was not passed, so rescue detail wrongly called the inspection endpoint

# Snowflake ID precision loss in JS Number
19-digit database snowflake IDs exceed JavaScript Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (2^53), so converting them with Number() corrupts the trailing digits and breaks backend lookups.

## Problem
- Converting a 19-digit id like `2117093674846941186` via Number() yields a rounded value (e.g. ...186 to ...200), so the backend reports the record as not found ("预警不存在")
- Two distinct templateItemIds can collapse to the same corrupted Number, producing duplicate items in the payload

## Fix
- Send all Long/snowflake IDs as strings in JSON; do NOT wrap them with Number() in the store or request layer
- Spring/Jackson coerces JSON strings to Long fields, so string IDs are accepted by the backend without change

## Verification
- After switching flood store payloads to String IDs, save and submit returned code=200 and detail echoed fill values correctly through the nginx proxy

# Nginx same-origin reverse proxy solves browser CORS
When an H5 app served from nginx calls a backend on a different origin, missing Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers block the calls; a same-origin nginx reverse proxy removes the need for backend CORS headers.

## Problem
- Direct browser calls from the nginx-served H5 to backend 9610 returned 200 but with no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header, so the browser blocked them
- OPTIONS preflight returned 403 with no CORS headers

## Fix
- Add nginx location blocks that proxy `/api-flood` to 9610 and `/api-auth` to 9211, so the H5 calls a same-origin path
- Set VITE_API_BASE_URL=/api-flood and VITE_AUTH_BASE_URL=/api-auth (relative, non-empty so the client config guard passes)
- Reload nginx with its correct prefix (e.g. `-p D:/nginx`) so the new config actually loads

## Verification
- After reload, `/api-flood` returned 200 JSON and `/api-auth` reached 9211 (400 on dummy body), confirming the proxy path works and CORS is solved
